title: Khronos TextureTransformTest -- KHR_texture_transform's offset, rotation and scale on six quads, each pointing at the marker that says which reading was used

criterion.says: The top row tests different combinations of the offset parameter with UV coordinates of `(0.0, 0.0)` to `(0.5, 0.5)` and offsets of `(0.5, 0.0)`, `(0.0, 0.5)`, and `(0.5, 0.5)` respectively from left to right, using the UV texture. A yellow image indicates that offset was not applied. ... The bottom left quad tests the rotation parameter with UV coordinates of `(0.0, 0.0)` to `(1.0, 1.0)` and a rotation angle of `0.392699` radians or `22.5` degrees, using the arrow texture. The green marker indicates the correct rotation. The yellow marker indicates the rotation was not applied. The red marker indicates the rotation was applied in the opposite direction. ... The bottom right quad tests offset, rotation, and scale at the same time. If everything is supported correctly, the arrow should point to the green marker.
criterion.note: Compare the transformed arrow direction with the vendor-defined green marker. Yellow denotes no transform and red denotes the reversed rotation. Histogram agreement cannot establish direction; inspect spatial agreement against the independently imported Cycles image. The engine implementation is not the oracle.

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (`board/`). This subject is twelve quads at two depths, so E is in the dozens and no single roll makes them rational together.

subjects.name: TextureTransformTest
subjects.notes: Twelve primitives over nine materials, and every one of them names ONE `baseColorTexture` -- so this asset decides whether the transform is composed and applied at all, and it cannot decide whether it is carried PER REFERENCE: no material here has a second textured socket to disagree with the first. That claim is held by `test/unit/gltf/EveryTextureReferenceCarriesItsOwnTransform.cpp`, because no asset in the Khronos corpus spells it. The primitives carry POSITION and TEXCOORD_0 and no NORMAL, so the subject draws through the emitted textured arm and the appearance is `baseColour(u,v)` alone.

source.pinReason: the same pin every other Khronos subject in this tree carries

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of board:0083 (src/gltf/Framing.h) applied to this subject's own bounds and to nothing else: azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 at r = 1.9391849572797033 m about the centre (0, -0.045633742881207695, 0.005), yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL, near = distance - r and far = distance + r. THE ROLL IS ZERO AND STATED: this subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so a roll would be a different draw of the same lottery rather than an exactness argument.
camera.note: The file carries no camera, so this case's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note: The only illumination is Blender's factory world, and it is left where it is because configuring it would be a second thing to keep honest.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: THE ORACLE IS LOWERED, NOT THE TOLERANCE (board:0087). This arm keeps exactly what the asset is for -- its own image, its uv set, its sampler and whatever the importer wired upstream of the Image Texture, which for this asset is the Mapping node `KHR_texture_transform` becomes -- and replaces only the closure. The lowering MOVES the subtree feeding Base Color rather than rebuilding it, so the transform crosses into the oracle for the same reason the base colour factor does. THE CLOSURE IS AN EMITTER AND NOT A DIFFUSE BSDF because the three markers stand 0.01 m in front of the quads they mark: at one sample per pixel a Diffuse BSDF there takes ONE cosine-weighted direction that either escapes to the world or meets a marker, so the marked quad would become a Bernoulli draw on the visible sky fraction and the case would be scoring an ambient-occlusion estimator (board:0087).

default.note: The 0.01-pixel box filter limits subpixel sampling spread but does not prove exact pixel-centre evaluation or agreement at discontinuities.

seed-shift.note: Measure sensitivity to the sample seed, including visibility and texture filtering at subpixel positions. Emission removes lighting-path variance but does not by itself guarantee bit-identical pixel samples.

notes: Exercises offset, rotation, scale and their composition on the pinned vendor geometry. Acceptance follows the extension's image-space rotation and vendor markers (the GLSL listing has the known sign error KhronosGroup/glTF#1563), not historical engine output. This asset does not establish independent transforms on multiple material sockets or texCoord overrides. Recompute image and geometry comparisons for each run; record results outside the manifest. Filtering discrepancies require separate diagnosis and do not justify disabling mipmaps or widening thresholds.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0, RE-HARVESTED after the camera became the framing rule's own answer (board:1398). Recomputed by the runner on every run and refused on mismatch, so this line PINS the framing and never chooses it; seeded from that recomputation, it is a drift detector rather than a present-error check.
